Client observations and retained ID match. Showing Not published violates P; retrying can create a second publication because the server does not deduplicate.

rationale: A reachable account state has no supported path to the promised recovery. Both ordinary login and access to support depend on authority available only through the permanently lost device.
decisive_trace_or_argument: Lose the sole trusted device permanently; attempt replacement login; approval requires that device. Attempt support; support requires login. With no recovery codes or alternate contact, no enabled supported action can obtain replacement authority.

limitations: This is a contract/design finding from supplied facts, not an executed test. It does not assume the device can be found or prescribe an unverified security policy.

rationale: The normal login dependency does not establish a defect because the supported public recovery path lies outside it and satisfies the qualified promise.

limitations: The conclusion is limited to published support hours and users able to complete verification; it implies no instant or unconditional recovery. The reported exercise was supplied, not rerun.

next_check: Control the real executor so cancellation application is delayed, and attempt delivery after Cancel success. Observe notification delivery, not merely the queued command. Preserving compatibility requires success only when the promised delivery barrier holds.
limitations: Analysis only; the trace is feasible by the supplied executor facts. It establishes a safety regression without making additional progress claims.

rationale: Pairwise overlap is insufficient. With identical observations, the component needs a single action safe across all three reachable configurations; their total intersection is empty.

limitations: The impossibility is scoped to one immediate guaranteed-safe choice with the supplied information and forbidden deferral. It does not apply if those constraints change. No execution was needed.

rationale: The controller rejects the obsolete callback before reducer delivery and performs the required cleanup. A callback arriving after cancellation is feasible but not itself a defect.
